newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY HIT BY SERIES OF DEMONSTRATIONS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY HIT BY SERIES OF DEMONSTRATIONS.

text.p: Traffic on several Hungarian roads in the country and in the capital was slowed on Saturday by demonstrations held by motorists, farmers and Budapest's communal service entrepreneurs, the police said.

Hundreds of vehicles blocked two lanes of the M5 motorway south of Budapest, in protest over what the drivers called unpayably high tolls and over the bad state and overburdening of other roads along the motorway.
"In Bacs-Kiskun county, near (town) Kecskemet, 177 vehicles and some 300 people took part in the demonstration," county police spokesman lieutenant-colonel Laszlo Ferenczi told Reuters.
The protesters demanded that the 850 forints ($4.85) fee for a 56 km stretch of the motorway should be halved, the Hungarian Radio said.
The government recently authorised the Ministry of Transport (KHVM) to start talks on reducing controversial tolls on motorways operated by private concessionary companies.
Hungary, expanding its motorway network, first introduced tolls last March, provoking protests of motorists and towns along the new roads.
KHVM commissioner Bela Szalai told the radio that the government would negotiate with the protesters but needed time to meet their demands.

In Budapest, 150 sewage-water trucks drove through the tourist districts of the city in a more than one kilometre long line as entrepreneurs protested over Budapest municipality's plans to centralize sewage water collecting.
The protesters were quoted by the radio as saying that the municipality wanted to pass the right of fluid waste collecting to its loss-making company.
Farmers' demonstrations continued on Saturday at several places in the country, a national police spokesman told Reuters, adding he did not know yet the number of participants.
Farmers, demanding the withdrawal of 1997 tax rules, blocked lanes of several roads with their vehicles every day in the past two weeks.
